, in the case of e + e − collisions, the threshold region is well accessible for the production of squark pairs and of gluinos, but that, for the production of stop pairs, it is only accessible for a small range of the stop mass.

the production cross sections for squarks and gluinos are calculable in the framework of perturbative QCP, provided the masses and decay widths are sufficiently large, but that the production of stops is calculable only in the limit where the mass of the stop is much larger than the mass of the top quark, and that in this case the production of stops in e + e − collisions is dominated by the production of the lighter stop.
the production of heavy SUSY particles is not necessarily a challenge to QCD, even if their decay widths are not very large.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
perturbative SUSY QCD is a good starting point for describing SUSY particle production near threshold, even in cases when the SUSY particle decay width is of the same order as the SUSY particle mass.

perturbative SUSY QCD is able to describe threshold production in the large width approximation, if the SUSY mass scale M SUSY ≲ 1 TeV and if the SUSY particle width is sufficiently large, Γ ≳ 100 GeV.
the production of SUSY particles in hadron-hadron collisions is dominated by gluons, which is in contrast to the case of electron-positron collisions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

for a large class of scenarios the production of stops at threshold is dominated by the production of the two heaviest squarks, which is a feature that can be exploited for the determination of the stop masses.

, in contrast to the case of heavy particles, SUSY particles with masses below 1 TeV and with a decay width above about 1% can be described in perturbative QED or QCD, respectively, if they are produced close to threshold.
, in the case of stop and gluino production, the non-relativistic expansion is not applicable at all.
